faq: Can it quote prices and discounts?
It can state the prices you give it. It cannot invent discounts, and we set clear rules for offers so it only mentions deals you actually run.
Will it push customers to buy?
No. It helps visitors choose, in a friendly tone. We avoid pressure tactics or false urgency, and it tells visitors when another product is a better fit.
Which calendars can it use for bookings?
Calendly, Google Calendar, Cal.com and most booking tools that give you a booking link or connection. We confirm your tool before you order.
Can it work with my store's product feed?
Often yes. Shopify, WooCommerce and similar stores can feed product names, prices and links in. For custom systems we confirm what is possible first.

desc:
A sales chatbot that helps visitors choose the right product turns browsing into a guided conversation. Ecom Swift LLC builds a sales assistant tuned to your real offers, which recommends, answers pre-purchase questions and offers a call when needed.

## What is a sales chatbot?

A sales chatbot is an assistant that talks with website visitors before they buy. It asks a few simple questions about their needs, recommends a product or plan, answers practical doubts and, when the purchase needs a person, offers to book a call. Its job is to help the visitor decide, not to push them.

This is different from a support bot. A support bot solves problems after the sale. A sales assistant works earlier, at the point where a visitor is comparing options and has not yet made up their mind.

## Why visitors leave without buying

Many visitors leave because they cannot tell which option fits them. A catalog with forty products, three plan tiers or several similar models forces the visitor to compare details on their own. If a question comes up, such as whether a size will fit or whether a plan includes a feature, they have nobody to ask, so they close the tab.

Contact forms are slow and email replies arrive after interest has faded. A chat window answers in the moment, while the visitor is still looking at the product.

## How a guided assistant helps conversions

The mechanism is simple: fewer doubts, shorter path. By asking two or three questions, the assistant narrows the choice and links straight to the right page. By answering pre-purchase questions on delivery, compatibility or terms, it removes the small obstacles that stop a decision.

For sales that need a conversation, such as services or high-value items, it captures a name and email and offers a booking link, so your team speaks to people who are already interested. Results depend on your offer, price and traffic, so we do not promise a specific increase. What the assistant removes is confusion.

## What a good sales assistant includes

- A short opening message that invites a question without interrupting.
- Two or three guiding questions about the visitor's need, budget range or use.
- Recommendations drawn from your real product or plan list.
- Direct links to the recommended product pages.
- Accurate prices and offers, taken from your data and never invented.
- Answers to pre-purchase questions on delivery, sizing, compatibility and terms.
- Calendar booking for sales that need a person.
- Name and email capture with clear consent wording.
- Leads sent to your CRM or spreadsheet.
- Answers to the objections customers raise most often.
- Bundle and upgrade suggestions that actually fit.
- Tracking of chats that lead to sales.

## What we do

We begin with your products, plans and the questions your sales team hears most. We turn these into a decision path: which questions to ask, which answers lead to which recommendation and when to offer a person.

Then we build and connect. The Basic package covers a small set of products with a short guided flow. The Standard package adds more products, booking links, lead capture and delivery of leads to your CRM or sheet. The Premium package covers a large catalog, answers objections, suggests bundles and upgrades, tracks chats through to sales and includes a tuning round after the first week.

We set firm limits. The assistant uses only prices and discounts that you supply. It does not invent offers, pressure visitors or make claims you cannot support. We test it on sample chats, including awkward ones, before launch.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the guiding questions few and easy to answer.
- Let visitors skip the questions and ask freely.
- Offer a human option for high-value or complex purchases.
- Update the product list whenever your range changes.
- Read the chats in the first week and adjust.

**Avoid:**
- Interrogating visitors with a long questionnaire.
- Letting the bot quote discounts that do not exist.
- Showing pop-ups on every page that cover the product.
- Capturing emails with no clear explanation of how they are used.
- Recommending the most expensive option every time.

## Who this service is for

It suits a store with many similar products where buyers often ask which one to pick. It suits a service business that wants visitors to book a call with the right person. It also suits a software or subscription seller with several plans that people struggle to compare.

## How to get started

Send us your product or plan list, current prices and the questions customers ask before buying. Tell us where leads should go and which calendar you use. We need access to your site and the chatbot tool as a collaborator, staff or developer user, never your passwords. You approve the flow before anything goes live.
